title: Project updates and status
lead: Is lesson ke baad tum standup aur client status call me kaam ka progress, pending cheezein, deadline aur delay clear English me bata paoge.
description: Week 5 English lesson: give project updates, say what is finished, what is in progress, and when it will be ready.

patterns.note: Kaam complete ho gaya, abhi result important hai.
patterns.negative: I haven't finished the contact page yet.
patterns.question: Have you finished the design?
examples: I've finished the testing for the login page.
Maine login page ki testing complete kar li hai.
She has finished the content update.
Usne content update complete kar liya hai.
patterns.grammar: Present perfect: have/has + past participle. Just-completed work with a present result. yet negative aur question ke end me.
patterns.mistake: “I have finish” → “I've finished.” have ke baad past participle.

patterns.say: I'm working on the payment page.
patterns.positive: I'm working on the payment page.
patterns.negative: I'm not working on that today.
patterns.question: What are you working on?
examples: I'm working on the mobile layout.
Main mobile layout par kaam kar raha hoon.
We're working on the final testing.
Hum final testing par kaam kar rahe hain.
patterns.grammar: Present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing. Abhi chal raha kaam.
patterns.mistake: “I working on it” → “I'm working on it.” be verb chahiye.

patterns.note: Kitna time lagega, simple duration me bolo.
patterns.question: How long will it take?
examples: It will take three hours to fix.
Ise theek karne me teen ghante lagenge.
The design will take one week.
Design me ek hafta lagega.
patterns.grammar: will take + time. Duration: two days / three hours. How long...? se poochho.
patterns.mistake: “It will take two days time” → “It will take two days.” days ke baad time nahi.

patterns.note: Kisi cheez par ruka hua kaam.
patterns.say: We are waiting for the content from the client.
patterns.positive: We are waiting for the content from the client.
patterns.negative: We aren't waiting for approval now.
patterns.question: What are we waiting for?
examples: We are waiting for the logo files.
Hum logo files ka wait kar rahe hain.
I'm waiting for your feedback.
Main aapke feedback ka wait kar raha hoon.
patterns.grammar: wait for + person/thing. Present continuous because wait abhi chal raha hai.
patterns.mistake: “We are waiting the client” → “We are waiting for the client.” wait for.

patterns.say: I'll send it by Friday evening.
patterns.positive: I'll send it by Friday evening.
patterns.negative: I won't send it before Monday.
patterns.question: When will you send it?
examples: I'll send the report by 5 p.m.
Main report shaam 5 baje tak bhej doonga.
We'll finish it by the end of the week.
Hum ise hafte ke end tak khatam kar denge.
patterns.grammar: by = deadline ke pehle ya us waqt tak. until = tab tak continuous. Deadline ke liye by.
patterns.mistake: “I'll send it on Friday” (deadline) → “I'll send it by Friday.” By = latest time.

patterns.note: Ek line me project ki position.
patterns.say: The current status is in review.
patterns.positive: The current status is in review.
patterns.negative: The current status is not clear.
patterns.question: What is the current status?
examples: The current status is in progress.
Abhi kaam chal raha hai.
The current status is on hold.
Kaam abhi ruka hua hai.
patterns.grammar: status is + noun/adjective. Common: in progress, in review, on hold, complete.
patterns.mistake: “The status is reviewing” → “The status is in review.” Status khud review nahi karta.

grammarRules: I'm working on the payment page.
We are waiting for the content.
status is + in progress / in review / on hold / complete
mistakes: It will take two days time.
We are waiting for the client.

pattern.model: I'm working on the payment page.
We are waiting for the content.

dialogue.context: Daily standup. Riya = project manager. Finished, in progress, blocked, deadline — chaar cheezein cover karo.

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.text: Quick update — where are we on the homepage?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: I've finished the design. I'm working on the mobile version now.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: It will take two days. We are waiting for the content from your team.

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.text: I'll send it today. Can you share a status update by Friday?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes, I'll send it by Friday evening. The current status is in progress.

dialogue.closing: Update ka formula: finished + in progress + blocked + deadline. Char lines, no story.

vocab.example: I'll send a status update by Friday.
There is a small delay in testing.
The page is ready for review.

selfCheck: Ek finished cheez “I've finished ___” se boli.
Ek current task “I'm working on ___” se boli.
Ek blocker “We are waiting for ___” se bataya.
Poora update 60 seconds me, bina story ke, bola.

pronunciation.title: -ed endings
pronunciation.body: finished = /ˈfɪnɪʃt/ (t sound); completed = /kəmˈpliːtɪd/ (id sound); moved = /muːvd/ (d sound). Teen alag endings suno.

pronunciation.title: Numbers and dates
pronunciation.body: two days, three hours, Friday the 30th. Numbers par stress, aur ‘th’ ko teeth ke beech se bolo.

pronunciation.title: Contractions
pronunciation.body: I've = /aɪv/, I'm = /aɪm/, I'll = /aɪl/. Fast speech me yahi natural hai.

pronunciation.title: Sentence stress
pronunciation.body: I've FINISHED the DESIGN. I'm WORKING on the PAYMENT page. Content words par stress.

followUps: Status update ka sabse short natural structure kya hai?
“I've finished” aur “I finished” me kya difference hai?
Delay batate time kya bolna chahiye?
Client ko deadline push karni ho to kaise bolun?
Mera standup update 60 seconds me fit ho raha hai?
mission: Send a 60-second status update in English — voice note ya real standup me.
